findings.title: Unhandled exception from token exchange leaks 500 instead of install error
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch at src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py line 423, safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data) is called outside any try/except, and get_user_info() on line 434 is also unprotected. If GitHub returns an error for a bad/re-used code, if the network fails, or if the user-info call returns 401, these helpers raise (e.g. ApiError/URLError). The PR description says invalid/re-used code should show the friendly github-integration-failed.html error, but instead the exception bubbles to a 500. This breaks the promised UX and can leak stacktraces.

findings.title: Direct metadata['sender']['login'] access crashes when sender missing
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch at src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py line 502, the code does pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. If integration.metadata has no sender key (e.g. integrations created via build_integration which only sets sender when state.get("sender") is present, legacy integrations, or deleted metadata), this raises KeyError resulting in a 500 during install instead of the intended error page. It also means the security check can never succeed for pipeline-created integrations that never persisted sender.

findings.title: build_integration never persists installer identity so check is ineffective
findings.body: In GitHubIntegrationProvider.build_integration at src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py line 376, sender is copied only if state.get("sender") exists. The new pipeline only binds installation_id and github_authenticated_user, never sender, so integrations created through the normal install flow have no metadata.sender stored. The later GitHubInstallation check against integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] therefore has nothing to compare against for those rows, defeating the user-mismatch validation for future reinstalls and guaranteeing the KeyError above.

findings.title: installation_id from query param overrides pipeline state
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch at src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py line 448, installation_id is resolved as request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id")). An attacker can complete OAuthLoginView for installation A (binding A and an authenticated user) then call the second step with ?installation_id=B to force validation/binding against a different installation. The stored pipeline value should take precedence or be required to match the query param, otherwise the OAuth identity can be paired with an attacker-chosen installation.

findings.title: OAuth token POST passes raw dict instead of encoded body
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch at src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py line 423, data is a Python dict {code, client_id, client_secret} passed directly as data= to safe_urlopen for https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token. The GitHub endpoint expects application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. The analogous OAuth2CallbackView url-encodes token params. Passing a dict risks wrong Content-Type/encoding and failed exchanges, causing valid installs to hit the Invalid installation request error.

findings.title: OAuth authorize redirect built without URL-encoding
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch at src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py line 408, the redirect is built by f-string interpolation of state and redirect_uri into the authorize URL without quoting. redirect_uri contains :// and / and state is a pipeline signature; unencoded values can break the query string or allow parameter injection if signature contains & or =. Use urllib.parse.urlencode for client_id, state and redirect_uri.
